BiblicalUsage: Nahum uses the word once, for the prancing horses and jumping chariots of Nineveh's fall. It is the restless, irregular movement of a warhorse in the noise of battle.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word belongs to judgment: the proud city's horses prance for the last time before it falls.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
